title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-maya-patel-inference-contract
content:
Quick scratchpad for redlines on inference contracts (hosted / dedicated / private). Mostly talking points & clauses to flag when reviewing customer/partner drafts.

Clauses to watch (priority):
- Liability / Cap: customer will push for uncapped liability or very high caps. Aim: cap = greater of $1M or fees paid in prior 12 months; carve-outs for IP indemnity, gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- Indemnity: customers often want us to indemnify broadly. Drive for narrow Redwood indemnity: IP infringement claims only (defend & indemnify). Customer to indemnify against claims arising from customer data, outputs misuse, regulatory fines.
- Limitation of damages: exclude indirect/consequential, but watch carve-outs they add (e.g., for data loss).
- Data rights / Training: absolute must: CUSTOMER owns Customer Data; Redwood gets a narrow license to process for providing service, telemetry/aggregated metrics only (opt-out for sensitive customers). No right to train or improve models on identifiable customer data without explicit opt-in.
- Data retention / deletion: default retention = 90 days for request logs; deletion on termination within 30 days (or acceptable alternative with retained backups for legal hold). For Private/VPC deployments, allow customer-managed retention and KMS.
- Security & compliance: require SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 (if enterprise asks). Pen test cadence (annual) and vulnerability disclosure policy. Breach notification: 72 hours from confirmation (customer expects 72h), include scope & remediation.
- Subprocessors / third parties: require notice & objection rights for new subprocessors; maintain current subprocessors list in Confluence.
- Audit rights: customers may ask for broad audit rights. Limit to remote evidence and annual audits with NDA, or SOC reports; on-site audits only for high-risk enterprise with scope/time-limited.
- SLA & remedies: customers push for strong uptime SLOs (e.g., 99.95%). Host SLA ok but push back on unlimited termination rights or large service credits. Remedy = service credits; carve-out for repeated breaches (escalation to execs). For Dedicated, include throughput/latency commitments and scheduled maintenance windows.
- Export controls / sanctions: include customer representation re: compliance with export laws and sanctions screening.
- Governing law / venue: customers often ask for their local law. Prefer CA or NY; push for alternative dispute resolution (mediation) then arbitration for enterprise to avoid injunction surprises.
- IP & outputs: clarify rights to model outputs: customer can use outputs, but cannot reverse-engineer Redwood models or claim model IP. For models provided by third parties (open weights), must pass through their license obligations to customer.
- Confidentiality: standard mutual NDA with 3-5 year duration post-termination for confidential information; sensitive customer data remains customer confidential.
- Insurance: require reasonable commercial liability insurance (e.g., $2M general liability; $2-5M cyber/E&O depending on account size).

Negotiation talking points (short):
- "We own the model and runtime IP; customers own their data and outputs. We'll not use identifiable customer data to train models without permission."
- "Retention default is 90 days for logs; we can offer reduced retention or on-prem options for regulated customers."
- "SLA remedies are service credits capped to fees in that month/quarter; termination for repeated violations after cure period."
- "We provide SOC2 Type II reports; for extra compliance customers can request contractually scoped audits with notice and reasonable limitations."
- "We limit indemnities to IP infringement and gross negligence; customers indemnify for data/misuse and regulatory claims."

Redwood-specific notes / things to check in drafts: 
- Distinguish between Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private: many clauses should change for Private (customer-managed infra, different data access, on-prem KMS).
- For Private installs, push for "customer-managed environment" language: Redwood obligations limited to shipped software/config and remote control plane only (if applicable).
- KMS / keys: ensure language allowing customer-managed KMS for Private; for Hosted, clarify Redwood's key management & HSM options and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) support.
- Telemetry & logs: redact PII by default; allow opt-out. Keep examples: prompt text might be sensitive — treat as Customer Data.
- Model variants & fallbacks: customer may want guarantees about model versioning/predictability. Offer stability commitments (pinned versions for Dedicated + rollover/upgrade windows).
- Performance metrics: for inference latency & throughput, prefer p90/p99 numbers in engineering addendum rather than in main contract.

Suggested short redlines (language snippets):
- Data / Training: "Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, improve, or further develop any machine learning model or service without Customer's prior written consent."
- IP Indemnity: "Provider will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims that Provider's services, as delivered, infringe any issued U.S. patent or copyright, provided Customer notifies Provider promptly and allows Provider to control the defense."
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, or IP indemnity, Provider's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) $1,000,000 and (ii) the fees paid by Customer to Provider under the applicable SOW in the 12 months preceding the claim."
- Confidentiality period: "Confidential Information will be protected for the Term and for three (3) years after termination (ten (10) years for trade secrets)."
- Deletion: "Upon Customer's written request following termination, Provider will delete Customer Data within thirty (30) days, except as required by law or for backups under a reasonable retention policy."

Open / unresolved questions to follow up internally:
- What's the standard liability cap we should propose for enterprise ($1M vs $5M)? Need input from finance for high ARR deals. (Action: legal + finance sync)
- Telemetry opt-out: can we build a simple opt-out toggle for enterprise customers? Engineering feasibility? (Action: ping infra & product)
- Retention defaults across products (hosted vs dedicated): confirm current defaults & any configurable knobs. (Action: product-ops)
- For Private/on-prem, what's our walk-away on support obligations (we're not responsible for customer infra). Need standard Private addendum paragraph. (Action: solutions-eng + customer-success)

References / templates:
- Confluence: Inference Contract Checklist (see linked artifacts).
- Example redlines: see GH-PR-342 (internal template for IP indems & data usage).

Notes to self: keep this doc loose — capture new negotiation language from deals and then consolidate into the legal playbook. If a customer insists on training rights, escalate to data-ops + product for commercial terms (explicit opt-in + premium).

-- Maya
